newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: IPB INTERESTS NOMURA, ING - DAILY.
newsitem.headline: IPB INTERESTS NOMURA, ING - DAILY.

text.p: Japan's Nomura and Dutch ING Bank have expressed the greatest interest in purchasing a minority stake in Czech bank Investicni a Postovni Banka a.s. (IPB) from the state, a Czech newspaper said on Saturday.
"Nomura and ING Bank are the most serious (parties) interested in the purchase of the state share," the daily Mlada Fronta Dnes quoted National Property Fund (NPF) chairman Roman Ceska as saying.
The NPF, the state privatisation agency, holds 31.5 percent of IPB which is one of the Czech Republic's "Big Four" banks.
The market price for that quantity of shares is roughly 5.3 billion crowns, the paper notes, adding however that experts believe a block sale would fetch a far higher price.
IPB shares were up five crowns at 301.0 on Friday.
Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik said on Friday that IPB should be the first of the Big Four, which control over 70 percent of Czech banking activity, to be privatised.
Kocarnik added that he would submit a plan to the government for further privatising the country's four largest banks within 14 days.

The four are Komercni Banka a.s., Ceska Sporitelna a.s., and IPB -- which have had some shares privatised through the government's voucher selloffs -- and Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka a.s., which is controlled through a variety of Czech and Slovak state institutions.
ING Bank has branch operations in the Czech Republic, while Nomura has so far maintained a representative office here.
Nomura was to have lead managed an issue of Global Depositary Receipts (GDR) for IPB, and sources at the Czech bank say the two companies enjoy close relations.

"We would be honoured by the opportunity to become a shareholder of Investicni a Postovni Banka," Mlada Fronta Dnes quoted Randall Dillard, general director of Nomura International for the region, as saying.
No one was avilable for comment at ING.
The paper added that "reliable banking sources" said negotiations between Nomura and officials of the Czech Finance Ministry and the NPF had intensified in the last 14 days.

IPB officially cancelled its GDR issue this week to avoid a clash with government plans to sell its stake to a "significant foreign strategic partner as a pilot project of full privatisation of large Czech banks", an IPB spokesman said.
The bank also cited higher-than-expected interest of current shareholders in the first round of an equity expansion scheme, leaving little left over for the GDR plan.
